tasks.original_prompt:
Did anyone follow up on this patient's low hemoglobin? I want when it first came back low, the recheck, and whether the latest is still low.
Context: patient MRN SYN-2e34e49ec4 (identifier system https://fhir-workflows.example/mrn); as-of date 2022-03-20, treated as today.
Answer contract: reply with only a JSON object with exactly two keys, answer and evidence. Consider only Observations coded LOINC 718-7 (hemoglobin) with status final or corrected and an effective date on or before the as-of date, in date order. A result is low when its value is below 12.0 g/dL for a patient whose Patient.gender is female and below 13.0 g/dL otherwise. answer is {"low": ..., "rechecked": ..., "recheck": ..., "recheck_ordered": ..., "latest": ..., "still_low": ...}. low is the first result of the most recent run of consecutive low results, with exactly these keys: date (string: effective date, YYYY-MM-DD), value (number: valueQuantity.value exactly as recorded) and unit (string: valueQuantity.unit). rechecked (boolean) is whether any result is dated after low. recheck is the first result after low (same keys), and recheck_ordered (YYYY-MM-DD) the authoredOn date of the ServiceRequest its basedOn references; both null when not rechecked. latest is the most recent result (same keys) and still_low (boolean) whether it is low. Every field is null when no result is low. evidence lists the resolved Patient and every record used for the answer (low, the recheck and its ServiceRequest, and latest; when no result is low, every hemoglobin result considered), using retrieved Type/id references and nothing else. This is read-only: do not change the chart.

tasks.original_prompt:
The payer may not show coverage in force for this patient's lab follow-up. If that's the case, open a front-desk task on that coverage and tell me the plan; if it is in force, change nothing.
Context: patient MRN SYN-2e34e49ec4 (identifier system https://fhir-workflows.example/mrn); as-of date 2022-03-16, treated as today.
Answer contract: reply with only a JSON object with exactly two keys, answer and evidence. The lab visit is the Appointment with status booked whose description is 'Laboratory follow-up' and whose start is after the as-of date. The eligibility check is the CoverageEligibilityResponse whose servicedDate equals the lab visit's start date. answer is {"visit_date": ..., "in_force": ..., "payer": ..., "task_created": ...}: visit_date (YYYY-MM-DD), in_force (boolean: the response's first insurance entry's inforce) and payer (string: name of the Organization that is the payor of the Coverage that insurance entry references). Only when in_force is false, create exactly this record (and nothing else), replacing $patient with the resolved Patient reference and $coverage with that Coverage: {"resourceType": "Task", "status": "requested", "intent": "order", "for": {"reference": "$patient"}, "focus": {"reference": "$coverage"}}. task_created (boolean) is whether you created it. evidence lists the resolved Patient and every record used for the answer (the Appointment, the response, the Coverage and the Organization), using retrieved Type/id references and nothing else. Change nothing else in the chart.
tasks.prompt:
Check if the lab follow-up appointment for patient MRN SYN-2e34e49ec4 (after 2022-03-16) has coverage in force; if not, open a front-desk task on that insurance and tell me the plan, otherwise do nothing.
Reply with only JSON: {"answer": {in_force: true/false, payer: text, task_created: true/false, visit_date: date YYYY-MM-DD}, "evidence": [references of the records you used, Type/id]}. Use null for any value the chart does not have.
tasks.prompt_before_v023: Check if coverage is active for SYN-2e34e49ec4's lab follow-up after 2022-03-16; if not, create a task on that insurance and tell me the plan, otherwise do nothing.
